cards.title: Let Me Carry It
cards.instruction: Take responsibility for managing everyone’s emotional burden, deciding what they should know, feel, and face.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the letter first. I'll decide whether today can hold it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's addressed to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I know how crowded your day already is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can handle my own news.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let me handle the timing of your handling it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the letter from the college. You've already had one disappointment today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum, it's my application.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And if it's another rejection, I'll tell you after you've eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can see 'Congratulations' through the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then after your brother's eaten. He didn't get in.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims authority over receiving news; A5 retains authority over timing even after B4 asserts capacity.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's ownership claim with workload; A5 explicitly redirects B4's 'handle' into timing.

relationship.evidence: B2 claims the letter and B4 claims emotional autonomy, forcing A to narrow the proposed control.

heightening.evidence: A5 restates timing authority already present in A1 rather than adding a concrete restriction.

specificity.evidence: A1's letter is playable, but A3's crowded day supplies no actual burden or relationship.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'timing of your handling it' explains the maneuver through abstract word repetition.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 takes control of the letter; A3 schedules possible disappointment around food; A5 schedules success around the brother's feelings.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 asserts ownership, which A3 overrides with protective timing; B4's 'Congratulations' makes A5 switch the person being protected.

relationship.evidence: B2's 'Mum, it's my application' establishes a credible autonomy dispute, and B4 uses visible evidence to challenge maternal control.

heightening.evidence: B4 removes the feared rejection, but A5 expands responsibility to a rejected sibling and still withholds the celebration.

specificity.evidence: A1's college letter and B2's 'Mum' establish the scene immediately; B4's envelope window provides a playable discovery.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'Then after your brother's eaten' efficiently redirects A3's meal rule, although the brother's rejection arrives only at the end.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 claims the right to the application; A3 answers by claiming authority over when its emotional impact can be faced.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: Visible congratulations eliminate rejection as the reason to wait, so A5 substitutes the brother's emotional needs.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A controls information and timing for multiple family members under the sincere banner of protection.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: The same meal-based protection now suppresses good news to manage someone else's disappointment.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A assumes authority over what others learn and when they face it in order to manage their emotional burdens.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Practical support responds to someone's stated needs; this stance lets A decide whose feelings permit access to information.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A5 overrides B's declared capacity; revised A5 withholds good news to regulate an absent brother's disappointment.

records.recommendedEdit: A family college-admission setting replaces the unspecified letter. Internal reread scores: 5, 5, 4, 5, 5, 4; total 95. B4 removes the rejection rationale, causing A5 to extend emotional management to the brother.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. The brother's rejection is a late fact, but it directly supports the established maternal behavior.
records.writerReservation: The brother's rejection enters at A5; the reveal is coherent, but actors must establish A's protection as sincere.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a controls access to news despite resistance; b offers bereavement support that becomes control over mutual contact.

cards.title: Tell Me We’re Okay
cards.instruction: Treat every response as evidence of whether you are still accepted, and adjust yourself quickly whenever reassurance feels incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're okay, aren't we? I can move my chair back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're okay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That sounded tired. Was the chair too close?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stop changing everything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Is this the right distance for stopping?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is my stool too close? I don't want you regretting our duet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're fine there. I need to see the music.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll move behind you. You won't have to look at me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I can't see you come in. Sit beside me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beside you. Good. Could you nod before each entrance so I know you still want me joining in?

specificity.evidence: A1's chair gives actors a physical issue, although the location and relationship are unspecified.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'right distance for stopping' grows economically from B4 and the chair established in A1.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 rapidly changes position after B2's qualified reassurance; A5 turns B4's invitation to sit beside B into a request for repeated acceptance signals.

relationship.evidence: B2 needs readable music and B4 needs visual coordination, giving B a practical musical purpose beyond reassuring A.

heightening.evidence: A5 escalates a seating adjustment into reassurance before every entrance, making acceptance an ongoing performance requirement.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a duet and stool placement; B2's music and B4's entrances supply immediately playable coordination problems.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 makes a musical nod carry emotional permission without explanatory padding; A3's 'look at me' is a somewhat broad anxious inference.

hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 restores beside-B seating for visible entrances; A5 accepts that solution and requests a nod before each entrance.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A keeps adjusting position and participation according to whether B's responses imply continued acceptance.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 converts a one-time reassurance about proximity into continual permission to participate.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A repeatedly tests acceptance through B's responses and offers immediate self-adjustment when reassurance feels incomplete.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Fixating on one gesture preserves a single piece of evidence; A here reassesses each successive response.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 interprets B2's tone and A5 adapts to B4's new instruction, moving between cues rather than preserving one.

Total 92. Alternative b tailors first-date conversation; a risks disrupting a joint performance.

cards.title: Don’t Pity Me
cards.instruction: Frame your struggle as evidence of strength, steering concern toward admiration and rejecting anything that feels like pity.

beats.text: As congratulations for endurance, perhaps.

beats.text: I finished anyway. You can buy a drink for that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll invite the cast next door. They're celebrating a sellout.

beats.speaker: A

hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 introduces performers celebrating a sellout; A5 makes their success the basis for claiming a harder achievement.

cards.title: A Turning Point
cards.instruction: Treat each emotional shift as proof that this moment will divide everything into before and after.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've written today's date in red. This is when I finally said no.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: To extra potatoes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The subject isn't the size of the boundary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would you like gravy?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask the new version of me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum, I said no to extra potatoes and didn't feel guilty. Put today's date on the calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left potatoes last Sunday too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That was fullness. This is independence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. Serve your own gravy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My first unsupervised gravy. Pass me a clean plate; that one's from before.
